language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, i am Chip!
Hi! My name is Kodi, I am a sled dog.
Sled dogs are dogs that are trained to pull a sled in cold, snowy places where the roads have not been built.
It's hard to drive a car or truck in the snow, but it is easy for dogs to pull a sled over snow.
Let’s figure out how far the sled dogs pulled the sled today.
They ran 4 miles before lunch and 3 miles after lunch. That’s 7 miles.
To get your answer, you can count on from a first number.
Or you can draw a picture.
You can also write the math equation down.
Or you can look for doubles. You can even use a number line.
Let’s add to see how far the sled dogs pulled the sled yesterday.
They ran 5 miles before lunch and 5 miles after lunch. How many miles did they run?
They ran 10 miles! Wow! Did you notice the two 5’s are doubles?  Good strategy!
Now it is your turn to practice adding! Have fun!
